_readme: Claims about jurisdictions outside South Africa. These sit in a separate file from facts.json for two reasons. First, facts.json is keyed by the bare figure and feeds GEO scoring, and several of these claims turn on numbers that mean something else elsewhere in the corpus (5% is a Mauritian registration duty here and an agent's commission on twenty other pages), so registering them there would hand unrelated articles a provenance they have not earned. Second, and the actual point: nobody on this project monitors the Portuguese State Budget, the Mauritian Economic Development Board or UAE tax practice the way we monitor SARS and the City of Cape Town budget. These figures will go out of date without anyone noticing. Each carries a reviewBy date; `npm run facts:review` fails once one is overdue, which is the whole mechanism. Reviewing means re-reading the primary source and either moving asOf and reviewBy forward or correcting every file listed.

claims.claim: Portugal applies a flat 7.5% IMT to non-resident purchasers, charged on the whole purchase price rather than on slices of it
claims.source: Portugal 2026 State Budget property tax provisions

claims.claim: Portuguese AIMI applies to property value above EUR 600,000 at 0.7% for individuals, rising to 1% above EUR 1 million, on top of ordinary municipal IMI
claims.source: Portuguese AIMI provisions, Codigo do Imposto Municipal sobre Imoveis

claims.claim: A leased Portuguese residential property can be exempt from AIMI where the rent stays at or below EUR 2,300
claims.source: Portuguese AIMI leased-property exemption provisions for 2026

claims.claim: The real estate route was permanently removed from the Portuguese Golden Visa in October 2023; the programme continues through funds, cultural support, research, job creation and business investment, so a Lisbon apartment confers no immigration benefit
Lisbon apartments averaged about 4.13% gross rental yield in August 2026, with districts spanning roughly 0.99% to 6.75%
claims.source: Lisbon rental yield market data, August 2026

claims.claim: An investment at or above the Economic Development Board threshold, commonly cited at USD 375,000, in a qualifying Mauritian scheme supports a residence permit for the buyer and dependants while the property is held
claims.source: Mauritius Economic Development Board residence permit criteria

claims.claim: A non-citizen may acquire Mauritian residential property only inside a state-approved framework: an active Property Development Scheme, legacy Integrated Resort Scheme or Real Estate Scheme stock, a qualifying Smart City project, or a ground-floor apartment scheme
claims.source: Mauritius non-citizen property acquisition frameworks, Economic Development Board

claims.claim: Mauritius charges a non-citizen 5% registration duty on a scheme acquisition, levies no capital gains tax on a property disposal, and charges the seller a 5% land transfer tax
claims.source: Mauritius Registration Duty Act and Land (Duties and Taxes) Act

claims.claim: The UAE dirham has been pegged to the US dollar since 1997, so a Dubai property is effectively a dollar-denominated asset earning dollar-linked rent
claims.source: UAE Central Bank dirham peg to the US dollar, in place since 1997

claims.claim: The UAE levies no personal income tax on rental income and no capital gains tax on an individual's property disposal, and runs no exchange control on funds entering or leaving
claims.source: UAE personal tax position for individuals, Federal Tax Authority

claims.claim: The United States taxes citizens and green card holders on worldwide income regardless of where they live, so a foreign rental property creates a US filing position that does not end when the owner leaves the country
claims.source: US Internal Revenue Code, taxation of citizens and residents on worldwide income

claims.claim: FBAR, FinCEN Form 114, is required when the aggregate value of all foreign financial accounts exceeds USD 10,000 at any point in the year; the property itself is not a financial account, but a South African bank account run for it is
claims.source: FinCEN Form 114 filing requirement, Bank Secrecy Act

claims.claim: FATCA reporting on Form 8938 covers specified foreign financial assets on thresholds that vary by filing status and by whether the taxpayer lives abroad, and sits alongside FBAR rather than replacing it
claims.source: IRS Form 8938 reporting requirement under FATCA

claims.claim: Real property located in the United States and real property located outside it are not like-kind to each other, so a section 1031 exchange cannot defer gain in either direction between a US property and a Cape Town one
claims.source: US Internal Revenue Code section 1031, domestic and foreign real property not like-kind

claims.claim: Double taxation agreements on the OECD model allocate the taxing right over income from immovable property to the state where the property sits, and Germany relieves that income by exemption with progression: it is outside the German tax base but still counted when fixing the rate on German income
claims.source: OECD Model Tax Convention article 6 and German exemption-with-progression method

claims.claim: Under German domestic law a gain on the private disposal of real property is taxable where the sale falls within a speculation period of ten years from acquisition, and outside the charge beyond it; business holdings are in a different regime
claims.source: German private disposal rules, ten-year speculation period for real property

claims.claim: The United Kingdom taxes residents on worldwide income and generally does not tax non-residents on foreign rental profit; residence is decided by a statutory test weighing days in the UK against connecting factors, not by nationality
claims.source: UK Statutory Residence Test and the residence basis of UK income tax

claims.claim: Where a UK resident owns South African property, the South Africa-United Kingdom double tax agreement relieves double taxation on the same rental profit by credit for the South African tax already paid, so the owner bears the higher of the two rates rather than both
claims.source: South Africa-United Kingdom double taxation agreement, credit relief

claims.claim: The United Kingdom charges non-residents a 2% stamp duty land tax surcharge and Singapore charges foreign buyers a 60% additional buyer's stamp duty; both are cited across this site only as the contrast with South Africa, which levies no foreign buyer surcharge at all
claims.source: UK non-resident SDLT surcharge; Singapore additional buyer's stamp duty for foreign buyers
